Sun Data Analytics helps clients combine quantitative summaries with qualitative evidence so findings are easier to inspect, explain, and use.

## Overview

Mixed-methods work is useful when numbers alone do not explain the full story, or when qualitative material needs structure before it can support decisions. The work can include transcript coding, open-ended response analysis, thematic summaries, survey analysis, group comparisons, and plain-language interpretation.

## Qualitative and Text Analysis

:::: {.index-list}
::: {.index-item}
### Transcript Coding

Prepare transcripts, build or apply codebooks, review coded excerpts, and summarize patterns across source material.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Open-Ended Response Analysis

Organize survey responses, interview notes, comments, or other text into themes, examples, and evidence tables.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Codebook Development

Create practical coding rules, definitions, examples, and review steps for qualitative or classification workflows.
:::
::::

## Quantitative Summaries

:::: {.index-list}
::: {.index-item}
### Descriptive Summaries

Summarize counts, shares, trends, distributions, and group-level comparisons.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Survey and Interview Synthesis

Connect structured survey results with interview themes, open-ended responses, or contextual notes.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Group Comparisons

Compare patterns across groups, time windows, source types, content categories, or respondent segments.
:::
::::
